program.build: cd risk && RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$HOME=~" cargo build -p pb-ol-probe --target wasm32-wasip2 --release
program.build_note: The remap keeps the builder's home directory out of the dependency panic paths that the binary embeds; two builds in a row gave the same hash. Without it the hash depends on the builder's home path.
program.imports: near:storage/api@0.2.0 plus wasi:cli, wasi:clocks, wasi:http, wasi:io, wasi:random (0.2.2 to 0.2.6; the worker's wasmtime 28 serves them)

versions.url_checked: downloaded back from FastFS; sha256 matches

versions.superseded_because: its `big` mode could not make an output under 329 bytes; hello, prices, calls and lock are the same code in both builds

notes: Use the Project source. The program imports near:storage/api, and the worker gives storage only to runs with a project uuid (worker/src/main.rs); a WasmUrl source would refuse to start ('WASM imports near:storage/api but storage is not configured'). From code, not run.
resource_limits must be present: omitting it makes the request compile-only (contract execution.rs: compile_only = params.compile_only || resource_limits.is_none()).
On chain the storage cell is the transaction signer's, so locks taken over HTTPS (the payment key owner's cell, pbf-keeper.testnet) are not visible to on-chain runs signed by another account.

Measured over HTTPS: hello uses about 0.23M instructions and 0.75 s; prices 32M and 2.5 s; calls n=200 8.3M and 6 s. 1B instructions and 20 s cover every mode except calls with n of about 500 or more.

payment_key_usd.covers: every HTTPS run in day1_outlayer_*.json, plus one smoke run whose result was not saved and the first build's big run

keeper_near.covers: two FastFS uploads, create_project and add_version (0.1 NEAR attached each, excess refunded)
